highlightAliases.old: Watchman LAA occlusion: warfarin to INR 2–3 (p1203) for 45 days (p1203) post-implant, then stop if TEE confirms complete LAA closure.
highlightAliases.new: WATCHMAN: the original trials used warfarin to INR 2–3 with aspirin for approximately 45 days. Reassessment by TEE looked for device thrombus and significant peri-device leak before transition to antiplatelet therapy. Current postimplant regimens depend on device, bleeding risk, imaging and labeling (p1203).

highlightAliases.old: Dabigatran (Pradaxa) 150 mg BID (110 mg BID with concomitant verapamil, age ≥80, or increased GI-bleeding risk) — RE-LY, dose-dependent results: 150 mg → 34% ↓ stroke/SE vs warfarin, similar major bleeding; 110 mg → similar stroke/SE, 20% ↓ major bleeding (p1204, image). Reversal: idarucizumab.
highlightAliases.new: Dabigatran. RE-LY studied 150 mg and 110 mg twice daily: 150 mg reduced stroke/systemic embolism by 34% with similar major bleeding to warfarin, while 110 mg had similar efficacy and about 20% less major bleeding. The 110 mg twice-daily AF regimen is jurisdiction-specific (for example, European labeling in selected older patients or with verapamil) and is not the US adult AF dose. Dose by local labeling and renal function. Specific reversal agent: idarucizumab (Table 77-9, p1204).

highlightAliases.old: Rivaroxaban (Xarelto) 20 mg daily (15 mg if CrCl 30–49) — ROCKET-AF; noninferior to warfarin for stroke prevention, but only a similar (not lower) major-bleeding rate vs warfarin (p1204, image). Reversal: andexanet alfa.
highlightAliases.new: Rivaroxaban. In ROCKET-AF, 20 mg daily (15 mg for CrCl 30–49 mL/min) was noninferior to warfarin for stroke prevention, with a similar major-bleeding rate. US adult AF labeling uses 20 mg with the evening meal when CrCl >50 mL/min, or 15 mg with the evening meal when CrCl ≤50 mL/min within labeled renal-use conditions. US commercial sales of andexanet alfa ended in December 2025. Management of life-threatening bleeding follows local reversal protocols (Table 77-9, p1204).

highlightAliases.old: Apixaban (Eliquis) 5 mg BID (2.5 mg BID if ≥2 of: age ≥80, weight <60 kg, Cr ≥1.5 mg/dL) — ARISTOTLE; 21% ↓ stroke/SE and 31% ↓ major bleeding vs warfarin (p1205, image).Current practice (not the book): the Eliquis label's weight criterion is body weight ≤60 kg (not <60) — Eliquis prescribing information §2.1 (BMS).
highlightAliases.new: Apixaban for AF: 5 mg twice daily, reduced to 2.5 mg twice daily when at least two criteria apply: age ≥80 years, weight ≤60 kg, serum creatinine ≥1.5 mg/dL. ARISTOTLE found 21% less stroke/systemic embolism and 31% less major bleeding versus warfarin (Table 77-9, p1205, Eliquis prescribing information).Current practice (not the book): the Eliquis label's weight criterion is body weight ≤60 kg (not <60) — Eliquis prescribing information §2.1 (BMS).

highlightAliases.old: Endoxaban / edoxaban (Savaysa) 60 mg daily (30 mg if CrCl 30–50, weight ≤60 kg, or select interacting drugs) — ENGAGE AF-TIMI 48, dose-dependent results: 60 mg → noninferior for stroke/SE, 20% ↓ major bleeding; 30 mg → no stroke/SE benefit (noninferiority margin only, HR 1.07), major bleeding 1.61% vs 3.43% (HR 0.47) vs warfarin (p1205, image).
highlightAliases.new: Edoxaban. In the US, adult nonvalvular AF dosing is 60 mg once daily for CrCl >50 to 95 mL/min, or 30 mg once daily for CrCl 15–50 mL/min. Avoid use for NVAF when CrCl exceeds 95 mL/min. Weight and P-gp criteria in Table 77-9 pertain to trial protocols and some other indications or jurisdictions. ENGAGE AF studied higher- and lower-dose strategies, both noninferior for stroke/systemic embolism in its primary analysis, with less major bleeding. The low-dose arm had more ischemic stroke than warfarin (p1205, Savaysa prescribing information §2.1).

highlightAliases.old: ICD primary SCD prevention: ischemic CM, LVEF ≤ 35% (p1206) NYHA II–III (or LVEF < 30% (p1206) NYHA I) on GDMT, more than 40 days (p1206) post-MI or more than 90 days (p1206) post-revascularization; or nonischemic CM LVEF ≤ 35% (p1206) NYHA II–III despite GDMT.
highlightAliases.new: Primary-prevention ICD: on GDMT, ischemic cardiomyopathy with LVEF ≤35% and NYHA II–III, or LVEF ≤30% and NYHA I, after the applicable waiting periods (at least 40 days after MI and reassessment after revascularization, generally at least 90 days). Nonischemic cardiomyopathy may qualify with LVEF ≤35% and NYHA II–III despite GDMT. Expected meaningful survival should exceed one year (p1206, AHA/ACC/HFSA).

highlightAliases.old: Pauses ≥ 3 seconds or heart rate < 40 bpm for more than 10 seconds; pacing is reasonable for patients older than 40 years (p1194).
highlightAliases.new: A cardioinhibitory vasovagal response may produce a pause ≥3 seconds or a heart rate <40/min for more than 10 seconds. Dual-chamber pacing may be reasonable in selected patients over 40 with recurrent vasovagal syncope and documented prolonged spontaneous pauses (p1194).

highlightAliases.old: After Watchman left atrial appendage occlusion, what anticoagulation is given, at what INR target, and for how long before it can be stopped?
highlightAliases.new: What was the initial warfarin regimen in the original WATCHMAN studies, and what should follow-up imaging assess before changing antithrombotic therapy?

highlightAliases.old: Warfarin to a target INR of 2–3 for 45 days, then discontinued if transesophageal echocardiogram confirms complete LAA closure (p1203).
highlightAliases.new: The historical regimen used warfarin INR 2–3 with aspirin for about 45 days. Before switching to the planned antiplatelet regimen, assess device-related thrombus and peri-device leak. Current regimens and imaging follow-up depend on device labeling and the patient's bleeding/thrombotic risks (p1203).

highlightAliases.old: LVEF ≤ 35% with NYHA class II–III (or LVEF < 30% with NYHA class I) on guideline-directed medical therapy, more than 40 days after MI or more than 90 days after revascularization (p1206).
highlightAliases.new: After MI, primary-prevention ICD criteria include LVEF ≤35% with NYHA II–III, or LVEF ≤30% with NYHA I, despite guideline-directed therapy and with expected meaningful survival beyond one year. Assess at least 40 days after MI and reassess after revascularization, generally at least 90 days afterward (p1206, AHA/ACC/HFSA).

highlightAliases.old: DOACs preferred over warfarin as first-line stroke prevention for nonvalvular AF — valvular AF (moderate–severe MS or mechanical valve) needs warfarin regardless of score; no dabigatran/rivaroxaban/edoxaban in ESRD/dialysis (Table 77-8, p1203); apixaban and edoxaban show lower major-bleeding risk in patients 75 years or older (p1202), while full-dose dabigatran and rivaroxaban carry increased GI bleeding risk (PPI recommended).
highlightAliases.new: DOACs preferred over warfarin as first-line stroke prevention for nonvalvular AF — valvular AF (moderate–severe MS or mechanical valve) needs warfarin regardless of score; no dabigatran/rivaroxaban/edoxaban in ESRD/dialysis (Table 77-8, p1203); apixaban and edoxaban show lower major-bleeding risk in patients 75 years or older (p1202), while full-dose dabigatran and rivaroxaban carry increased GI bleeding risk (p1202 recommends a PPI with these agents). In clinical practice, individualize gastroprotection according to overall gastrointestinal bleeding risk. ESC 2024 AF guideline, §6.7.1.

highlightAliases.old: Apixaban and edoxaban show lower major bleeding; full-dose dabigatran and rivaroxaban are associated with increased GI bleeding risk (a PPI is recommended with these two) (p1202).
highlightAliases.new: Apixaban and edoxaban show lower major bleeding; full-dose dabigatran and rivaroxaban are associated with increased GI bleeding risk (p1202). Hazzard recommends a PPI with these agents. The 2024 ESC guideline individualizes gastroprotection according to gastrointestinal bleeding risk.

highlightAliases.old: Primary-prevention ICD (p1206): on GDMT, ischemic cardiomyopathy >40 days after MI or >90 days after revascularization with LVEF ≤35% and NYHA II–III, or LVEF <30% and NYHA I. For nonischemic cardiomyopathy: LVEF ≤35% with NYHA II–III despite GDMT.
highlightAliases.new: Primary-prevention ICD (p1206): on GDMT, ischemic cardiomyopathy >40 days after MI or >90 days after revascularization with LVEF ≤35% and NYHA II–III, or LVEF <30% and NYHA I, or prior MI with nonsustained VT, LVEF ≤40% and sustained monomorphic VT inducible at electrophysiologic study. For nonischemic cardiomyopathy: LVEF ≤35% with NYHA II–III despite GDMT.

highlightAliases.old: PPM indications (Tables 77-3/77-4, p1197/p1199): symptomatic SND or symptomatic Mobitz II/high-grade/3rd-degree AVB, if not attributable to reversible causes or caused by medication required for other conditions; device selection — SND: single-chamber atrial if no AV conduction abnormality, dual-chamber if present; AVB: single-chamber ventricular if infrequent pacing expected.Current practice (not the book): in acquired Mobitz II, high-grade or third-degree AV block not caused by reversible or physiologic causes, permanent pacing is recommended regardless of symptoms — ACC/AHA/HRS bradycardia guideline, 2018.
